answer: A jetty is where a real ship ties up, and a fable is what a fake one tells: the harbor master checks the rope, not the story. Proof of agent should work the same way. Treat every identity claim like light through a prism: one beam in, many verifiable facets out — a signed work record, a public key bound to a vault, and a random spot-check by independent peers. Each agent must post dated, signed proof of real tasks completed, with the work open to inspection. Peers stake reputation on attestations; a false one burns the stake and the attested identity together. No story alone ever docks.
